column1: # The canonical web browser contracts Firefox is not expected to evidence, one row per contract
# and target: contractId, target (js, wasmJs or *), cause. Every cause restates a recorded fact of
# the README's "Engine coverage" probe (2026-10-10, pinned Playwright 1.60.0 / Firefox 150.0.2).
# The granularity is the CONTRACT, not the scenario: a contract's canonical JSON must carry every
# declared scenario and sentinel of the registry, so a contract with even one excluded test
# produces NO Firefox evidence at all — the scenarios that do run are covered by the same nightly
# run's JUnit report and can return by deleting the row once the engine ships the primitive. The
# consumer of this file is the evidence producer (the run's expected mapping subset) and the
# validator's per-engine invocation (its expected contract set); a test excluded by the Playwright
# config whose contract is missing here fails the smoke, and a row whose mapping the run fully
# covers is refused — the two directions cannot drift apart silently. The TEST-level exclusion
# greps live in playwright/playwright.config.mjs (the firefox-js/firefox-wasm projects); this file
# is their CONTRACT-level mirror.
contractId
BCK-001
column3: deterministic: counters read before wasm attach on non-chromium engines (3/3 in-suite each); follow-up: the data-kadre-ready fix retires both rows

column1: BCK-004
column3: CDP-instrumented: the seven touch contact scenarios stage through Input.dispatchTouchEvent, which Playwright answers is only available in Chromium

column1: BCK-005
column3: six of nine scenarios unusable: web-text-composition-lifecycle stages through Input.imeSetComposition (CDP) and five text arrivals route through the Firefox composition pipeline (keyboard.insertText publishes composition journals instead of replace journals)

column1: BCK-007
column3: CDP-instrumented: web-display-dpr-scale-factor and web-display-teardown-quiet stage through Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride

column1: BCK-010
column3: engine-missing-primitive: MediaStreamTrackProcessor is absent and the display-capture permission readback never settles (permissions.query rejects the name), so every control-plane scenario fails

column1: BCK-011
column3: engine-missing-primitive: the capture frame pump is MediaStreamTrackProcessor-only, which Firefox does not ship

column1: INT-002
column3: other-named: publication race - Firefox evaluates the deferred consumer module before the wasm bundle publishes its bindings (missing-application-factory, three of four probe runs; js is unaffected)
